title: Validation & Canary Dashboard for Batching/Caching Recommender Service
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Background: We are building a recommender service that suggests batching and prefix/KV cache configurations per customer route/workload to lower cost and improve throughput. Before we auto-apply recommendations at scale, we need a repeatable validation pipeline that runs canary experiments, collects fidelity and economic metrics, and exposes a single dashboard for cross-variant analysis and safe rollback triggers.

Objectives: 1) Create an experimentation scaffold for validating a recommended config vs baseline on live traffic using conservative canary splits. 2) Surface cost and quality KPIs on a dedicated dashboard with per-route breakdowns and statistical significance markers. 3) Implement automated safety gates for staged rollout and automatic rollback when regressions or anomalies are detected. 4) Produce a runbook and telemetry contract so other teams can onboard new recommendation policies.

Design/Experiment Plan: - Assignment: stable hashing by customer_id + route to ensure consistent variant for a given session. Canary traffic schedule: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 40% -> 100% with manual approval gates at each step. Each step runs for minimum 30 minutes, but can extend to meet sample size thresholds. - Variants: Baseline (current config) vs Rec-v1 (recommended batching/kv parameters) vs Rec-v1+AggressivePrefetch (optional third arm for internal testing). - Metrics collected per-request: latency P50/P90/P99 (ms), tokens/sec, GPU utilization (%), cost_per_request (estimated $), cache_hit_ratio (%), KV_evictions_per_min, model_quality_score (percent pass on canonical eval promptset), error_rate (5xx, decoding failures). - Success criteria: Cost reduction >= 9% at stable 95% CI without model_quality_score drop > 1.5 percentage points and without error_rate increase > 0.1pp. Tail latency P99 must not exceed baseline by more than 15%.

Telemetry & Instrumentation: - Add tags: experiment_id, variant, recommendation_id, route, customer_tier. - Ensure per-token accounting hooks emit cost estimates and batching window stats (avg_batch_size, batch_wait_ms). - Log sample decoded outputs for the evaluation promptset with unique sampling ids for offline quality checks. - Expose aggregated time-series to Cortex/Prometheus with 1m and 5m resolution, and push event-level data to our analytics warehouse for significance testing.

Dashboard Spec: - Top-level summary: current canary split, live savings estimate, rolling 95% CI for cost delta, and safety gate status. - Panels: (1) Cost per 1000 tokens by variant; (2) Latency distribution overlays (P50/P90/P99) with historical baseline; (3) Cache hit ratio and KV eviction rate; (4) Model quality pass rate and example regression bucket; (5) Traffic & sample size progression; (6) Auto-rollback triggers and recent incidents. - UX: allow filtering by route, recommendation_id, customer_tier, and time window; show raw event counts and z-score for each metric. - Links: canonical experiment details page (Confluence), PRs, and the deploy that applied the config.

Automation & Safe Apply/Rollback: - Safe-apply workflow: when Rec-v1 passes canary gates, the controller will auto-promote to next split percentage. The controller will only promote if sample-size requirements are met and no safety gate tripped in last 10 minutes. - Rollback triggers: automatic rollback if any of the following occur during a promotion window: (a) model_quality_score drop > 1.5pp with p<0.05, (b) error_rate up >0.1pp vs baseline, (c) P99 latency increase >15% sustained for 5m, (d) cache_hit_ratio drops by >10% and GPU utilization increases by >12%. - On rollback, the controller will pin traffic back to the last-known-good variant and create an incident with pre-filled diagnostics. Engineers can annotate and re-run after adjustments. - Safety gates include a circuit-breaker to cap concurrent promotions to 3 globally to limit blast radius.

Analysis Plan: - Use bootstrap and permutation tests where normality assumptions fail; compute 95% CIs for cost delta and test equivalence on quality metrics. - Statistical engine will flag metrics with insufficient power; experiments failing to meet power requirements must be extended. - Produce a regression report with sampled outputs for any quality anomalies; route-level analysis to identify traffic slices at risk.

Acceptance Criteria: - Dashboard populated with live data for at least 3 internal routes and one external customer pilot. - Automations can promote from 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% in fully automated run for an internal route. - Alerts and rollback work end-to-end (trigger, rollback, incident creation). - Documentation: Confluence guide and runbook for how to add a new recommendation policy.

Risks & Mitigations: - Risk: small but important customer segments could be under-represented. Mitigation: stratified sampling option and manual opt-out for high-value customers. - Risk: noisy telemetry leads to false positives. Mitigation: require sustained anomalies and multi-metric confirmations before rollback.

Next Steps: 1) Land instrumentation PR for experiment tags and event-level logging. 2) Implement controller state machine and promotion logic. 3) Build dashboards per spec and onboard two internal routes for pilot. 4) Schedule stakeholder review and legal/security sign-off for customer pilots.
